---
title: Wiki Tool Reliability — Fix CLI + MCP Bugs
type: spec
tags: [spec, cli, mcp, tooling, bugs]
---

## Overview

Multiple bugs in the MCP tool handlers (`wm_page.*`, `wm_index`) and CLI commands (`wm-cli page`) break agent workflows daily, forcing filesystem fallback and violating the MCP-first principle. Root cause in MCP is match-arm patterns that silently discard fields. CLI is missing the `update` command and has path-resolution inconsistencies.

The project follows an **AI-agent-first** model — CLI page commands exist for MCP tool handlers, not interactive human use. All content I/O is via stdin.

## Locked Decisions

- D1: Scope covers ALL wiki tool reliability bugs — MCP (match arms, id confusion, undocumented params) + CLI (no update, multiline content, meta.path relative) + wm_index
- D2: Fix + refactor to typed handler pattern that prevents field discarding + regression tests per bug
- D3: Remove `--content` flag, always use stdin for page content
- D4: CLI must be invoked from wiki root. `meta.path` always resolved relative to CWD (which IS the wiki root)
- D5: Add `wm-cli page update` subcommand
- D6: `page create` and `page update` accept content via stdin only (no `--content` flag)
- D7: Include wm_index reliability bugs in scope
- D8: Each bug fix must include integration + regression tests
- D9: Canonical parameter is `id`. Remove `page_id` entirely. No deprecation period.
- D10: Error format — wire the existing `From<ToolError> for ErrorData` conversion in transport.rs so code, message, and hint flow through JSON-RPC error.data
- D11: Handler pattern — BOTH exhaustive match (deny `_` across all arms) AND handler-level destructuring
- D12: Split `wm_index` into 3 separate tool registrations: `wm_index_rebuild`, `wm_index_status`, `wm_index_embed`

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**FR-1: Fix MCP match-arm discarding**
In `mcp/tools/page.rs` and `mcp/tools/index.rs`, fix all pattern matches using `_` to discard fields. Each field must be explicitly bound. Apply double protection: (a) exhaustive match arms that name every field, (b) destructure at handler function body top so compiler warns on unused.

**FR-2: Fix `page_id` / `id` parameter confusion**
Remove `page_id` parameter entirely. Canonical parameter is `id`. Update all MCP tool handlers and JSON schemas.

**FR-3: Wire ErrorData conversion in transport**
Wire the existing `From<ToolError> for ErrorData` impl in `wm-error` into `transport.rs` so MCP error responses include `code`, `message`, and `hint` as structured JSON-RPC error.data.

**FR-4: Split wm_index into separate tools**
Replace single `WmIndexAction` tagged enum with 3 separate tool registrations: `wm_index_rebuild`, `wm_index_status`, `wm_index_embed`. Each has its own handler, its own input struct, and no hidden `action` discriminator.

**FR-5: Add `wm-cli page update` subcommand**
New CLI command that accepts JSON via stdin with optional fields. Mirror of MCP `wm_page.update`.

**FR-6: Stdin-only content input**
Remove `--content` flag from `page create`. Both `page create` and `page update` accept content exclusively via stdin.

**FR-7: Path resolution consistency**
All CLI page commands resolve `meta.path` consistently relative to CWD (wiki root per D4).

**FR-8: Add missing input JSON schemas**
All MCP page tool parameters must have complete JSON schemas.

**FR-9: Regression tests per bug**
Each bug in the bug list has a dedicated integration + regression test that fails before the fix and passes after.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- NFR-1: All existing integration tests must pass
- NFR-2: Each bug fix includes a regression test
- NFR-3: MCP error responses include structured code/hint (not just message)
- NFR-4: Tool signatures show correct parameter names (not hidden discriminators)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `wm_page.update` with `tags` field correctly sets page tags
- [ ] AC-2: `wm_page.*` tools accept `id` parameter (not `page_id`)
- [ ] AC-3: MCP error responses include `code` and `hint` fields (not just message)
- [ ] AC-4: `wm_index_rebuild`, `wm_index_status`, `wm_index_embed` are 3 separate callable tools with no hidden `action` param
- [ ] AC-5: `wm_index Embed` handler reads `force` parameter (not discarded)
- [ ] AC-6: `wm-cli page update <id>` reads JSON from stdin and updates page correctly
- [ ] AC-7: `wm-cli page create` with stdin content creates page with correct multiline body
- [ ] AC-8: `wm-cli page link/update/delete` resolve paths correctly from CWD
- [ ] AC-9: No match-arm uses `_` to discard action fields in page or index tool handlers
- [ ] AC-10: Each bug (B1–B8) has a regression test
- [ ] AC-11: All existing integration tests pass
- [ ] AC-12: All MCP tool JSON schemas show required parameters correctly

## Bug List

| # | Tool | Symptom | Root Cause |
|---|------|---------|------------|
| B1 | `wm_page.update` | `tags` parameter silently ignored | Match arm: `tags: _` |
| B2 | `wm_page.*` | Phantom "page not found" on update | Lookup mismatch between get/update service layer |
| B3 | `wm_page.*` | `page_id` vs `id` parameter confusion | Ambiguous naming |
| B4 | `wm_page.*` | Missing required parameter schemas | Undocumented in JSON schema |
| B5 | `wm-cli page` | No `update` command | Never implemented |
| B6 | `wm-cli page` | `--content` breaks on multiline | Flag not suitable for multiline |
| B7 | `wm-cli page link/update/delete` | `NOT_FOUND` — path resolved wrong | `meta.path` relative to wrong base |
| B8 | `wm_index` | Hidden `action` discriminator required | Tagged enum not split into separate tools |
| B9 | `wm_index Embed` | `force` parameter silently ignored | Match arm: `force: _` |
| B10 | Backend | Error format drops code/hint | Transport not wired to ErrorData conversion |

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Agent updates page tags
**Given** an agent calls `wm_page.update` with `{ "id": "my-page", "tags": ["rust", "async"] }`
**Then** the page's tags are set correctly (not silently discarded)

### Scenario 2: Agent calls wm_index tools
**Given** an agent calls `wm_index_rebuild` with `{ "skip_embed": true }`
**Then** the tool works without requiring a hidden `action` discriminator

### Scenario 3: Agent receives structured error
**Given** an agent calls `wm_page.get` with a nonexistent `id`
**Then** the error response includes `code: "NOT_FOUND"` and a `hint` field

### Scenario 4: Agent creates page with multiline content
**Given** an agent pipes multiline content via stdin to `wm-cli page create`
**Then** the page is created with the complete multiline body
